A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRPE research despite the changed title and organization. Their complete text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original exploration and downstream policy-learning experiments in secret-room and two-agent Reacher environments, including supplementary results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: TRPE retains the same single-trial objectives, per-agent importance sampling, gradient updates, and KL trust region. Inlining the former IS-Optimizer subroutine changes the pseudocode presentation, not the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use secret-room and two-agent Reacher for reward-free exploration and subsequent sparse-reward learning. The stronger unsupervised-pretraining framing introduces no additional evaluated task or domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain joint, disjoint, and mixture objective variants and the same uniform/random initialization controls. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported discretization, exploration horizons, policy architectures, and TRPE/MA-TRPO hyperparameters remain unchanged. v3 does not report a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The horizon comparisons, state-visitation heatmaps, and policy-entropy analyses are retained. v2's appendix Figures 4–5 become v3's Figures 3–4 without additional analytical experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and 95% confidence intervals over four runs and specify four seeds in the implementation appendix. No uncertainty-estimation practice or repeated-run count changes.

E6.justification: The empirical plot data and visitation images match across versions: v2 Figures 2–5 correspond to v3 Figures 1–4. Curves, bar heights, uncertainty bands, and the reported comparative findings are retained.

T1.justification: The main bounds and most proofs remain unchanged. However, the final derivation in v2 Lemma A.7/v3 Lemma B.7 replaces E[Var]+Var[E] with E[Var+E], introducing an incorrect identity. Section 3 also adds an explicit mixture-entropy decomposition into average marginal entropy and KL divergence.

C1.justification: v2 claims to introduce convex Markov games as a novel class, while acknowledging concurrent work later. v3 explicitly attributes that framework to Gemp et al. and positions its contribution as extending it to task-agnostic exploration and unsupervised MARL. This materially narrows the foundational novelty claim while retaining the algorithmic and empirical claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds explicit limitations concerning Monte Carlo sample inefficiency, obstacles to Bellman-based methods, and the discrete-space restriction of plug-in entropy estimation. The explanation connecting harmful disjoint pretraining to nearly deterministic policies becomes more tentative.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports Apple M2 hardware, 8 GB memory, and a maximum execution time of 24 hours. Existing hyperparameters and the repository link remain unchanged. Its downstream-results caption no longer specifies v2's three-goal count for Reacher.

R1.justification: The rewritten related work substantially broadens coverage of swarm robotics, intrinsic motivation, and unsupervised pretraining, including URLB and additional pretraining methods. It also revises the relationship to Gemp et al., contrasting their centralized, infinite-trials focus with this work's decentralized, single-trial approach.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten around unsupervised pretraining. A four-question roadmap replaces the contribution list, several explanations are condensed, and related work and the Lipschitz assumption move into the appendices.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The conceptual distribution diagram is removed, experimental figures are resized and rearranged, and the two-part pseudocode becomes one boxed, numbered procedure. These are substantial visual changes despite unchanged empirical graphics.

improvement.justification: v3 provides clearer novelty qualifications, broader research context, and useful limitation and hardware disclosures. However, it introduces an incorrect variance identity in the final proof of Lemma B.7, where v2 retained the variance-of-conditional-mean term. With the methods and empirical evidence unchanged, these benefits and the mathematical regression do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
